items.title: 53279_Lee Young Oral History Interview
items.q: I worked under a guy at Warner Brothers, Ray Heinrichk

ctx.x: whatever she would happen to be doing, I would take the baton and I would conduct the band, and when you're that age, you don't really realize what you're doing -- especially if you're a percussionist, you know, you don't really realize what you're really doing. Not what you're really doing -- I guess I'm trying to say how important it is; what it may mean later on.

And when I started conducting for Nat, it was really a simple thing, and the guys thought that I had been conducting for ages, but I had not. And then again, I had worked under so many good conductors, you know -- I worked under both Bachalegnakoffs, you know, I worked under Morris Stoloff, I worked under a guy at Warner Brothers, Ray Heinrichk, George Estolle, Johnny Greene, by the time I was with Nat, I had worked under all these people -- Johnny Greene and George Estolle, and Phil Moore was not bad, either.
He did some conducting at RKO Studios when he would make the arrangements. Were you aware of that?
